shortDescription: Audiosrv logs 10317 when the audio service encounters an unhandled exception.
fullDescription:
10317 from Windows Audio (audiosrv) indicates a crash in an audio endpoint, often caused by a buggy APO (Audio Processing Object) from the chipset vendor (Realtek, Nahimic, SonicSuite).

Disabling 'Audio enhancements' on the device, updating or rolling back the audio driver, and removing 3rd-party audio tools resolves most reports.

fixSteps.title: Disable enhancements
fixSteps.instruction: Sound > Playback device > Properties > Enhancements tab > 'Disable all enhancements'.

fixSteps.title: Update audio driver
fixSteps.instruction: Device Manager > Sound > Update driver.

fixSteps.title: Restart Audio services
fixSteps.instruction: services.msc > restart Windows Audio + Windows Audio Endpoint Builder.

whenToCallPro: When all DIY steps fail.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Error 0x887A0006 — DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG
shortDescription: The graphics device has stopped responding because of an in-application error.
fullDescription:
0x887A0006 returns to games and DirectX apps when the GPU hangs under workload. TDR (Timeout Detection and Recovery) kicks in; if the app doesn't handle device-removed events, it crashes.

Root cause is usually an unstable GPU overclock, driver bug, or a specific game shader. TdrDelay registry extension gives the GPU more time but masks rather than fixes the problem.

fixSteps.title: Remove GPU overclock
fixSteps.instruction: Reset to stock in MSI Afterburner or GPU vendor tool.

fixSteps.title: Increase TDR delay
fixSteps.instruction: regedit > HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\GraphicsDrivers — DWORD TdrDelay = 10 (seconds).

fixSteps.title: Clean reinstall driver
fixSteps.instruction: DDU + latest WHQL.

whenToCallPro: When all DIY steps fail.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Error 0xC000007F — Disk Full / Insufficient Resources
shortDescription: STATUS_DISK_FULL returned to applications trying to allocate storage or pagefile.
fullDescription:
0xC000007F indicates the volume is out of space or the quota is exhausted. This affects pagefile growth, temp file creation, and some apps' save operations.

Free 10–20% of the system drive, remove large hidden files (hiberfil.sys, pagefile.sys overage), and verify there's no quota limit on the user.
symptoms: Very little free space on C:

fixSteps.title: Run Storage Sense
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > System > Storage > Cleanup recommendations.

fixSteps.title: Disable hibernation (if unused)
fixSteps.instruction: powercfg /h off — frees hiberfil.sys.

fixSteps.title: Remove old shadow copies
fixSteps.instruction: vssadmin delete shadows /for=c: /oldest (repeat).

fixSteps.title: Check quota
fixSteps.instruction: File Explorer > C: Properties > Quota tab.

whenToCallPro: When all DIY steps fail.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Task Scheduler 0x80041316 — RPC Server Unavailable
shortDescription: Task Scheduler cannot contact the Schedule service.
fullDescription:
0x80041316 appears in Task Scheduler UI or when running tasks programmatically. The Schedule service (schedule) is stopped, its dependencies failed, or DCOM blocked the call.

Start the Task Scheduler service and its dependencies (RPC, DCOM launcher) and retry.

fixSteps.title: Start Schedule service
fixSteps.instruction: services.msc > Task Scheduler > Start + Automatic.

fixSteps.title: Start dependencies
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure RPC and DCOM Server Process Launcher running.

fixSteps.title: Reset DCOM
fixSteps.instruction: dcomcnfg > verify Enable DCOM.

whenToCallPro: When all DIY steps fail.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Task Scheduler Last Run Result 0x1 — General Failure
shortDescription: A scheduled task returned exit code 1, indicating the program failed.
fullDescription:
0x1 (result code 0x00000001) is the application's own exit code, not a Task Scheduler error. The task launched successfully; the command inside returned 1.

Check the Action's program, arguments, and Start in folder. Run the exact command manually to reproduce.

fixSteps.title: Run manually
fixSteps.instruction: Open cmd, cd to Start-in, run the exact program and arguments.

fixSteps.title: Set Start in
fixSteps.instruction: Task Properties > Actions > Edit > fill 'Start in (optional)' with full path.

fixSteps.title: Use Run with highest privileges
fixSteps.instruction: General tab > check 'Run with highest privileges' if elevation needed.

whenToCallPro: When all DIY steps fail.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Event ID 3104 — Windows Search Failed to Load
shortDescription: Windows Search (SearchIndexer.exe) could not load required plugin or index.
fullDescription:
3104 indicates a protocol handler failed to load (commonly the MAPI handler for Outlook search). Index rebuild or Outlook reinstall is usually needed.

If Outlook search returns no results, this event is the first place to look.
symptoms: No search results in Start menu

fixSteps.title: Rebuild index
fixSteps.instruction: Indexing Options > Advanced > Rebuild.

fixSteps.title: Re-register Outlook MAPI
fixSteps.instruction: In Outlook, File > Options > Search > Indexing Options > Advanced.

fixSteps.title: Reset Windows Search
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Apps > Windows Search > Advanced options > Reset (via Get-AppxPackage on older builds).

whenToCallPro: When all DIY steps fail.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Event ID 219 — Driver Failed to Load
shortDescription: Kernel-PnP logs 219 when a driver cannot load for a specific device.
fullDescription:
Event 219 lists the driver name and device instance that failed. Common with outdated USB filter drivers, leftover drivers from uninstalled devices, or drivers not signed for current Windows build.

Identify the driver in Device Manager (yellow triangle) and update or remove it.

causes.cause: Driver not compatible with current Windows build

fixSteps.title: Identify driver
fixSteps.instruction: Event 219 details lists driver name.

fixSteps.title: Update in Device Manager
fixSteps.instruction: Device Manager > update driver for yellow-triangle device.

fixSteps.title: Remove phantom devices
fixSteps.instruction: Device Manager > View > Show hidden devices > uninstall greyed entries.

whenToCallPro: When all DIY steps fail.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Error 0x8007007E — The Specified Module Could Not Be Found
shortDescription: ERROR_MOD_NOT_FOUND when loading a library or COM component.
fullDescription:
0x8007007E is returned when LoadLibrary fails because the DLL itself or one of its dependencies is missing from the search path. Common during Explorer shell-extension loading, scheduled tasks that call rundll32, and after incomplete uninstalls.

Process Monitor with 'NAME NOT FOUND' filter identifies the exact missing file.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall the application
fixSteps.instruction: Most reliable fix if a specific app throws it.

fixSteps.title: Use Process Monitor
fixSteps.instruction: Filter for NAME NOT FOUND to find the missing DLL path.

fixSteps.title: Restore Visual C++ runtimes
fixSteps.instruction: Reinstall all VC++ Redistributables.

whenToCallPro: When all DIY steps fail.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Windows Defender Update Failed 0x80240022
shortDescription: Windows Defender/Security definition update failed with 0x80240022.
fullDescription: Error 0x80240022 appears in Windows Security when Defender tries to download the latest definitions via Windows Update but the update engine reports WU_E_ALL_UPDATES_FAILED. It is usually caused by a corrupted Windows Update cache, stuck SoftwareDistribution folder, or interference from a third-party antivirus.

causes.cause: BITS or Windows Update service stopped

symptoms: Protection definitions are out of date banner

fixSteps.title: Reset Windows Update cache
fixSteps.instruction: Stop wuauserv and bits, rename C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution to .old, restart services.

fixSteps.title: Manually download signatures
fixSteps.instruction: Download mpam-fe.exe from Microsoft Security Intelligence page and run it.

fixSteps.title: Remove third-party AV
fixSteps.instruction: Uninstall competing antivirus and retry update.

whenToCallPro: If definitions still won't update after cache reset and manual install.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Windows Defender Service Error 0x800704E7
shortDescription: Defender service fails to start with ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS 0x800704E7.
fullDescription: 0x800704E7 (ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS) from Windows Defender means a duplicate instance or leftover registration is preventing Defender from starting. Often seen after removing a third-party AV that didn't fully deregister, or after a botched Defender update.
symptoms: Virus & threat protection page shows error
Real-time protection toggled off and greyed

fixSteps.title: Run removal tool
fixSteps.instruction: Use the vendor's official removal tool for the previous AV (e.g., Norton, McAfee, Avast cleanup).

fixSteps.title: Re-register Defender
fixSteps.instruction: Run: "%ProgramFiles%\Windows Defender\MpCmdRun.exe" -ResetPlatform

fixSteps.title: SFC and DISM
fixSteps.instruction: Run sfc /scannow and DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth.

whenToCallPro: If Defender still fails to start after cleanup and system scans.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: svchost.exe High CPU Usage
shortDescription: One or more svchost.exe processes consume 50-100% CPU continuously.
fullDescription: svchost.exe hosts many Windows services; when one service inside it misbehaves, Task Manager shows svchost.exe with sustained high CPU. Common offenders: Windows Update (wuauserv), Superfetch/SysMain, Connected User Experiences (DiagTrack), Windows Search. Expand the process in Task Manager to see grouped services.

fixSteps.title: Identify the service
fixSteps.instruction: Task Manager > Details > right-click svchost.exe > Go to services. Note which services are grouped.

fixSteps.title: Reset Windows Update
fixSteps.instruction: Stop wuauserv, clear SoftwareDistribution, restart.

fixSteps.title: Disable SysMain if on SSD
fixSteps.instruction: services.msc > SysMain > Disabled.

fixSteps.title: Run full malware scan
fixSteps.instruction: Windows Security > Full scan.

whenToCallPro: Persistent high CPU after all services disabled one by one.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Windows Modules Installer Worker (TiWorker.exe) High CPU/Disk
shortDescription: TiWorker.exe consumes CPU and disk for long periods.
fullDescription: Windows Modules Installer Worker services pending update component operations. Spikes are normal after updates but should subside within 30-60 minutes. If sustained for hours, the component store may be corrupted.

causes.cause: Large cumulative update installing in background
Stuck pending operation from failed update

symptoms: Fan loud for hours after update

fixSteps.title: Wait 60 minutes
fixSteps.instruction: Allow post-update servicing to complete.

fixSteps.title: Run DISM
fixSteps.instruction: dism /online /cleanup-image /restorehealth

fixSteps.title: Clear pending.xml
fixSteps.instruction: Boot to Recovery, rename C:\Windows\WinSxS\pending.xml to .old.

whenToCallPro: If CPU remains pegged >24h and DISM fails.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Registry Editor Cannot Import File
shortDescription: regedit shows 'Cannot import X.reg: Error accessing the registry'.
fullDescription: This error appears when importing a .reg file if the file encoding is wrong (ANSI vs UTF-16), the first line does not contain 'Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00', the user lacks permission on target keys, or the file is corrupted.

causes.cause: File saved as ANSI instead of UTF-16
Permission denied on target registry key

symptoms: Partial import - some keys written, others fail

fixSteps.title: Check the header
fixSteps.instruction: First line must be exactly: Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00

fixSteps.title: Re-save as UTF-16 LE
fixSteps.instruction: Open in Notepad, Save As > Encoding: Unicode.

fixSteps.title: Run regedit as admin
fixSteps.instruction: Right-click regedit > Run as administrator, then File > Import.

fixSteps.title: Take ownership of target key
fixSteps.instruction: regedit > right-click key > Permissions > Advanced > change Owner.

whenToCallPro: If import still fails on a critical key after taking ownership.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Error Loading .reg File
shortDescription: Windows shows 'The specified file is not a registry script' when opening a .reg.
fullDescription: Windows refuses to load the file because it does not match the expected registry script format. The file extension is correct but the content is HTML, plain text, or wrong encoding. Exports from Windows 9x era (REGEDIT4 header) are also accepted but often misformatted.

causes.cause: File is actually a text file renamed

fixSteps.title: Open in Notepad
fixSteps.instruction: Right-click > Open with > Notepad. Check first line.

fixSteps.title: Fix header
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure line 1 is 'Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00' (no leading spaces).

fixSteps.title: Save as UTF-16
fixSteps.instruction: File > Save As > Encoding: Unicode.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: WMI Error 0x80041032 — Call Cancelled
shortDescription: WBEM_E_CALL_CANCELLED returned from a WMI query or provider.
fullDescription: 0x80041032 occurs when a WMI call is cancelled, often because the provider timed out or the calling process was terminated. Seen in scripts using Get-WmiObject, in SCCM client health, and in MMC snap-ins.
symptoms: Scripts using WMI hang then error

fixSteps.title: Restart Winmgmt service
fixSteps.instruction: net stop winmgmt && net start winmgmt

fixSteps.title: Verify repository
fixSteps.instruction: winmgmt /verifyrepository

fixSteps.title: Rebuild if inconsistent
fixSteps.instruction: winmgmt /resetrepository (last resort).

whenToCallPro: If repository rebuild is needed and applications break.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: WMI Access Denied 0x80041003
shortDescription: WBEM_E_ACCESS_DENIED when querying WMI namespace.
fullDescription: 0x80041003 indicates the calling user lacks Remote Enable, Execute Methods, or similar WMI permissions on the namespace (typically root\cimv2). Common in remote monitoring tools running as a non-admin service account.

causes.cause: UAC filtering the token for local admin

fixSteps.title: Run as administrator
fixSteps.instruction: Elevate the calling process or script.

fixSteps.title: Grant WMI permissions
fixSteps.instruction: wmimgmt.msc > Properties > Security > select namespace > Security > add user with Remote Enable + Execute Methods.

fixSteps.title: Check DCOM config
fixSteps.instruction: dcomcnfg > My Computer > Properties > COM Security > grant Launch/Activation.

whenToCallPro: If permissions are managed by GPO and cannot be changed locally.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: WMI Repository Corrupted
shortDescription: winmgmt /verifyrepository reports 'WMI repository is not consistent'.
fullDescription: The WMI repository (C:\Windows\System32\wbem\Repository) has become inconsistent. This blocks security software, Group Policy processing, Event Viewer in some views, and many management tools.

fixSteps.title: Verify
fixSteps.instruction: winmgmt /verifyrepository

fixSteps.title: Attempt salvage
fixSteps.instruction: winmgmt /salvagerepository

fixSteps.title: Reset if salvage fails
fixSteps.instruction: winmgmt /resetrepository (will break third-party management agents).

whenToCallPro: If reset is needed in a managed enterprise environment.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Microsoft Store Error 0x80073CF9
shortDescription: Microsoft Store fails to install or update apps with 0x80073CF9.
fullDescription: 0x80073CF9 means Store cannot create the WindowsApps staging folder or ran out of permissions to write there. Often caused by a moved Apps install location, corrupted AppX repository, or missing C:\Program Files\WindowsApps folder.

causes.cause: New apps install location set to a removed drive

fixSteps.title: Reset Store cache
fixSteps.instruction: Run wsreset.exe.

fixSteps.title: Reset install location
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > System > Storage > Advanced > Where new content is saved > set to C:.

fixSteps.title: Re-register Store
fixSteps.instruction: PowerShell (admin): Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers *WindowsStore* | Foreach {Add-AppxPackage -DisableDevelopmentMode -Register "$($_.InstallLocation)\AppXManifest.xml"}

whenToCallPro: Persistent 0x80073CF9 after re-registration.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Microsoft Store Error 0x80070002 — File Not Found
shortDescription: Store install/update fails with 0x80070002 (system cannot find the file specified).
fullDescription: In the Store context, 0x80070002 usually means a required AppX package dependency or a staging file is missing. Often hit after an interrupted update, or when AppReadiness service is disabled.

fixSteps.title: Restart Store services
fixSteps.instruction: Restart AppXSvc, ClipSVC, AppReadiness.

fixSteps.title: wsreset
fixSteps.instruction: Run wsreset.exe.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall the problem app
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Apps > select app > Uninstall, then reinstall from Store.

whenToCallPro: If reinstallation fails repeatedly.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Store/Update Error 0x80240017 — Update Not Applicable
shortDescription: 0x80240017 returned when an update or Store package is not applicable.
fullDescription: WU_E_NOT_APPLICABLE (0x80240017) is reported when the system does not meet a prerequisite for the package: missing parent update, wrong architecture, or locale mismatch. The user sees it most often when trying to install a MSU or Store app that requires a newer Windows build.
symptoms: Store app install fails with same code

fixSteps.title: Install latest SSU
fixSteps.instruction: Install the latest Servicing Stack Update for your build.

fixSteps.title: Check Windows build
fixSteps.instruction: winver - compare to app/update requirements.

fixSteps.title: Install via Update Assistant
fixSteps.instruction: Use Windows Update Assistant if a feature update is required.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Microsoft Store Error 0x803F7000
shortDescription: Store license acquisition failed with 0x803F7000.
fullDescription: 0x803F7000 is a licensing error: the Store client couldn't validate the app license against the account, often because the date/time is wrong, the Microsoft account is signed out, or Licensing Service is stopped.

causes.cause: Microsoft account not signed in to Store

symptoms: Owned apps won't install on this PC

fixSteps.title: Fix date and time
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Time & Language > Date & Time > Set automatically.

fixSteps.title: Sign out and back in
fixSteps.instruction: Store > profile icon > Sign out > Sign in with MS account.

fixSteps.title: Start Licensing services
fixSteps.instruction: services.msc > start Windows License Manager and ClipSVC.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: OneDrive Error 0x8004DE40 — Can't Connect
shortDescription: OneDrive cannot connect to sign-in servers.
fullDescription: 0x8004DE40 signals a connectivity failure to Microsoft's auth servers. Usually a proxy, TLS, or DNS issue on the client, or temporary MS service outage.

fixSteps.title: Check internet
fixSteps.instruction: Browse to https://onedrive.live.com - must load.

fixSteps.title: Disable proxy/VPN
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Network > Proxy > off. Disconnect VPN.

fixSteps.title: Enable TLS 1.2
fixSteps.instruction: Internet Options > Advanced > check TLS 1.2.

fixSteps.title: Reset OneDrive
fixSteps.instruction: %localappdata%\Microsoft\OneDrive\onedrive.exe /reset

whenToCallPro: If corporate proxy blocks MS sign-in endpoints.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: OneDrive Error 0x8004DE85 — Account Mismatch
shortDescription: OneDrive account does not match, can't sign in.
fullDescription: 0x8004DE85 means the credentials supplied don't match the account OneDrive expects (e.g., school/work account vs personal). Often after a tenant change or account rename.
symptoms: OneDrive link in sync client fails

fixSteps.title: Unlink account
fixSteps.instruction: OneDrive > Settings > Account > Unlink this PC.

fixSteps.title: Clear cached creds
fixSteps.instruction: Control Panel > Credential Manager > remove OneDrive/MicrosoftOffice entries.

fixSteps.title: Re-sign in
fixSteps.instruction: Launch OneDrive, sign in with the correct account.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: OneDrive Sync Error 0x8004DEA6
shortDescription: OneDrive stuck on 'Processing changes' with 0x8004DEA6.
fullDescription: 0x8004DEA6 usually points to a protocol or server-side mismatch during sync — often triggered by a file with invalid characters, a path over 400 chars, or a conflict the client cannot reconcile.

fixSteps.title: Check OneDrive error list
fixSteps.instruction: Click OneDrive cloud icon > see list of problem files.

fixSteps.title: Rename offending files
fixSteps.instruction: Remove : * ? " < > | # % and shorten path.

fixSteps.title: Reset OneDrive
fixSteps.instruction: onedrive.exe /reset

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Windows Search Not Working
shortDescription: Start menu search returns no results or hangs.
fullDescription: Search may fail because the SearchUI/SearchApp process is frozen, the index is corrupted, or the Windows Search service is stopped. In Windows 10/11 with Cortana integration, a broken SearchUI is the most common cause.
symptoms: Typing in Start menu shows nothing

fixSteps.title: Restart SearchApp
fixSteps.instruction: Task Manager > kill SearchApp.exe / SearchHost.exe; they auto-restart.

fixSteps.title: Rebuild index
fixSteps.instruction: Control Panel > Indexing Options > Advanced > Rebuild.

fixSteps.title: Start the service
fixSteps.instruction: services.msc > Windows Search > Start, Automatic.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Windows Search Indexer Stopped
shortDescription: SearchIndexer.exe is not running; index is stale.
fullDescription: Windows Search service (WSearch) launches SearchIndexer.exe. If service crashed or was disabled, the index never updates and Outlook/File Explorer search return partial or no results.
symptoms: Outlook shows 'Search performance will be impacted'

fixSteps.title: Start service
fixSteps.instruction: services.msc > Windows Search > Startup type Automatic (Delayed) > Start.

fixSteps.title: Rebuild index
fixSteps.instruction: Indexing Options > Advanced > Rebuild.

fixSteps.title: Reset ACLs on search folder
fixSteps.instruction: icacls %programdata%\Microsoft\Search /reset /t /c

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Windows Search Disabled
shortDescription: Search feature disabled by policy or registry.
fullDescription: Group Policy (AllowCortana, AllowSearchToUseLocation, DisableSearch) or the Windows Search feature itself may be turned off. Some 'debloat' scripts disable it permanently.

fixSteps.title: Restore feature
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Apps > Optional features > Add feature > Windows Search.

fixSteps.title: Remove GPO
fixSteps.instruction: Local Group Policy Editor > Computer Configuration > Admin Templates > Windows Components > Search > set policies to Not Configured.

fixSteps.title: Re-enable services
fixSteps.instruction: Start WSearch and SearchHost services.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Bluetooth Not Turning On
shortDescription: Bluetooth toggle greyed out or doesn't enable in Settings.
fullDescription: Occurs when the Bluetooth driver crashed, the radio is disabled in BIOS/UEFI, airplane mode forced it off, or a Windows Update broke the driver. Quick Action tile also disappears.
symptoms: Bluetooth toggle missing from Quick Actions
Device Manager shows yellow triangle on Bluetooth

fixSteps.title: Toggle airplane mode
fixSteps.instruction: Turn on, wait 10s, turn off.

fixSteps.title: Run Bluetooth troubleshooter
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other > Bluetooth > Run.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall driver
fixSteps.instruction: Device Manager > Bluetooth radio > Uninstall device (check Delete driver) > restart > Windows reinstalls.

fixSteps.title: Check BIOS
fixSteps.instruction: Reboot to UEFI, confirm Bluetooth/wireless is enabled.

whenToCallPro: If driver reinstall and BIOS checks fail.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Bluetooth Device Unpaired Unexpectedly
shortDescription: Previously paired BT device disappears and won't reconnect.
fullDescription: Windows may drop pairings after driver updates, profile corruption, or when a device is also paired to another host (phone). Removing and re-pairing usually fixes it.

causes.cause: Fast Startup interfering with BT stack

symptoms: Device shown as 'Paired' but not connected
Cannot connect to previously known headphones

fixSteps.title: Remove and re-pair
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Bluetooth > select device > Remove; then pair again.

fixSteps.title: Reset the device
fixSteps.instruction: Factory reset the BT device (headphones usually: hold power 10s).

fixSteps.title: Disable Fast Startup
fixSteps.instruction: Power Options > Choose what power buttons do > uncheck Fast Startup.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: HDMI 'No Signal' on External Monitor
shortDescription: External display connected via HDMI shows 'No Signal'.
fullDescription: Caused by cable/port failure, wrong input selected on monitor, GPU not outputting to that port, or a HDCP handshake failure. Common after sleep/resume cycles.

causes.cause: Integrated GPU disabled in BIOS while using onboard port

fixSteps.title: Select correct input
fixSteps.instruction: Monitor OSD > Input > HDMI1/2.

fixSteps.title: Swap cable and port
fixSteps.instruction: Try another HDMI cable and a different port on GPU.

fixSteps.title: Force projection mode
fixSteps.instruction: Press Win+P > Duplicate or Extend.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall GPU driver
fixSteps.instruction: DDU in Safe Mode, reinstall latest driver.

whenToCallPro: If multiple cables and ports fail — likely hardware.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Second Monitor Not Detected
shortDescription: Windows Settings Display page doesn't show the second screen.
fullDescription: Windows may miss a second monitor because of EDID read failures, a disabled output on the GPU, missing drivers, or a docking station passthrough issue.

causes.cause: Docking station firmware out of date

symptoms: Only one display listed in Settings

fixSteps.title: Click Detect
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > System > Display > Multiple displays > Detect.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cable
fixSteps.instruction: Power off monitor, unplug, wait 15s, replug.

fixSteps.title: Update GPU driver
fixSteps.instruction: Download latest from NVIDIA/AMD/Intel.

fixSteps.title: Update dock firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Vendor utility (DisplayLink, Dell, Lenovo).

whenToCallPro: If hardware swap tests indicate port or dock failure.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: File Explorer Crashes Repeatedly
shortDescription: explorer.exe crashes when opening folders or right-clicking.
fullDescription: Usually a shell extension from a third-party app (backup, cloud storage, archiver) is faulty. Can also be caused by corrupted thumbnail cache or a bad network drive mapping.

fixSteps.title: Clear thumbnail cache
fixSteps.instruction: cleanmgr > Thumbnails.

fixSteps.title: Use ShellExView
fixSteps.instruction: Run NirSoft ShellExView, hide Microsoft-signed, disable remaining suspects one at a time.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect stale drives
fixSteps.instruction: File Explorer > This PC > right-click any red X drive > Disconnect.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Quick Access Not Loading
shortDescription: File Explorer shows 'Working on it...' forever at Quick Access.
fullDescription: Quick Access hangs when one of the pinned locations is a dead network share, OneDrive is offline, or the AutomaticDestinations cache is corrupted.
symptoms: Green bar crawls across address bar

fixSteps.title: Set This PC as default
fixSteps.instruction: Folder Options > Open File Explorer to: This PC.

fixSteps.title: Clear jumplist cache
fixSteps.instruction: del /f /q "%appdata%\Microsoft\Windows\Recent\AutomaticDestinations\*"

fixSteps.title: Unpin dead items
fixSteps.instruction: Right-click Quick Access pin > Unpin from Quick Access.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.a: Usually fixable with standard troubleshooting steps.

title: Recycle Bin Corrupted
shortDescription: 'The Recycle Bin on C:\ is corrupted. Do you want to empty it?'
fullDescription: The $Recycle.Bin folder on a drive has a damaged index file. Windows will offer to rebuild; accepting deletes whatever is inside.
symptoms: 'Do you want to empty it?' prompt on every boot

fixSteps.title: Reset from CMD
fixSteps.instruction: Run as admin: rd /s /q C:\$Recycle.bin (repeat per drive letter).

fixSteps.title: chkdsk
fixSteps.instruction: chkdsk C: /f on next reboot.
